name: Ashley Mugwambi
summary: I build and run enterprise software for critical institutions in Zimbabwe. Since February 2022 I have been Lead Programmer at ZESA Holdings (ZETDC), where I lead a team of eight developers and own the architecture and operation of the Business Excellence System, used by more than 8,000 people nationally.

My work covers the full life of a system: designing business workflows, building web, mobile and API solutions, testing them, releasing them, securing them, tuning their performance and supporting them in production.

Outside work I write open-source Rust: five crates on crates.io and an npm package, built to the same standard as production code, with property tests, benchmarks against the popular alternatives, CI on Linux, Windows and macOS, and a security policy.

cases.title: Filling an abandoned gap in Rust
cases.context: fuzzy-matcher, used by 481 crates and downloaded 10 million times every 90 days, has not been updated since 2020.
cases.action: Built fuzzrank with a 64-bit character fingerprint per line, a bounded heap for top results and tight alignment for highlights; benchmarked it against fuzzy-matcher and nucleo on 16k real paths; ported the inquire prompt library to it and ran its full test suite.
cases.result: 11–14× faster than fuzzy-matcher with the same matches; inquire's 292 tests pass on the published crate. A gap found during the port (empty patterns) was fixed and released the same day.

cases.title: Safer, faster releases
cases.context: Releases needed checking before going live, with a way back if something failed.
cases.action: Rebuilt the pipeline around a staged copy with checks, migrations, tests and automatic rollback; ran tests in parallel and fixed the flaky tests that exposed.
cases.result: Failed releases roll back on their own, and release test time fell from about 22 minutes to about 8.

cases.title: Testing what users actually run
cases.context: SQLite-only runs hid faults, and UI faults had passed a fully green backend suite.
cases.action: Added MySQL test runs, React render tests and a jsdom harness that exercises page scripts and buttons.
cases.result: The MySQL runs exposed hidden faults, and testing now reaches browser-side behaviour.

cases.title: Closing access gaps
cases.context: An external EY penetration test required remediation.
cases.action: Led the remediation and enforced login across the platform.
cases.result: Closed an anonymous API endpoint and 195 pages reachable without sign-in.

cases.title: Finding a root cause in the data
cases.context: A blank column had been reported.
cases.action: Wrote a master-data health check that runs at every deployment.
cases.result: Its first run found the real cause: 20,718 materials had no unit of measure.
